summary: Relative Fargues-Fontaine curves and period geometry, first part: the ramified Witt coefficients, the integral period space and its annuli, the Frobenius quotient giving the curve, the divisor moduli with their completed rings, and the twists with the graded algebra. Refined to declaration granularity from the reviewed integrated decomposition, keeping all 20 node identifiers whose stage lies in this part's scope with their statements, hypotheses, proof steps, acceptance items and verified locators, and adding prerequisites resolved to the pinned libraries or to a named supplier stage, planets, per-layer coverage, and API outlines with unit tests for the two definitions and six constructions. ALL FOUR sources were downloaded again in this session and all four SHA-256 hashes reproduce the recorded values byte for byte. The library search found more here than in any sibling roadmap: Mathlib supplies WittVector.teichmuller, which is exactly the multiplicative section the first node asserts; WittVector.fontaineTheta, whose kernel the primitive degree-one ideals are; PreTilt and PreTilt.untilt; IsAdicComplete and AdicCompletion; IsDiscreteValuationRing, which is what B^+_dR is at a geometric untilt; GradedAlgebra, ProjectiveSpectrum and LocallyRingedSpace, which is the exact level at which the map to the algebraic curve is asserted. What is absent is the adic-space and perfectoid layer itself, and that is exactly what the twenty-one requests ask for. The packet keeps the two things the roadmap insists on: the integral space RETAINS the special fibre V(pi), and the map X_S -> X_S^alg is constructed formally with NO ampleness hypothesis, the equivalence being another roadmap's theorem. Eight gaps are recorded, seven carried and one added. Two structural proposals: two atlas edges inside this roadmap run against the source's proof order, and the ramified Witt foundations have no owner.

declarations.provides: Witt vectors. W_{O_E}(R^+) is the ring whose Spa, minus a vanishing locus, IS the integral period space; everything in this part is built on it.
The Frobenius endomorphism of the Witt vectors. The phi whose quotient defines the curve, and the sigma of the isocrystals, are this map.

The multiplicative section [.] : R -> W(R). This is exactly the section the ramified-Witt universal property asserts, and it is what [varpi] means in the definition of the integral period space and in the radius function.

Fontaine's theta as a ring homomorphism W(R-flat) -> R. The divisor of a leg is cut out by a generator of ker(theta_i), and the primitive-degree-one-ideal correspondence is about its kernel; the pinned library already has the map.

The tilt as an inverse limit along Frobenius. The base S is the tilt of its untilts, and the perfectoidness statement after base change to O_{E_infty} identifies the tilt with the perfectoid open unit disc.
The untilt map out of the tilt, the pinned form of the correspondence between untilts and the base that the functor-of-points theorem is about.
The perfection functor. R^+ is perfect, which is the hypothesis making the Witt lift flat and the Teichmueller section unique.
Perfect rings of characteristic p, the hypothesis of the ramified-Witt universal property.

Adic completeness. W_{O_E}(R) is pi-adically complete by the universal property, W_{O_E}(R^+) carries the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology, and B^+_dR is the completion along the divisor ideal; all three are statements at this level.
The adic completion functor itself, the operation that produces B^+ from the structure sheaf along the divisor ideal.
Discrete valuation rings. At a geometric untilt B^+_dR is a complete DVR with residue field the untilt, which is where the Cartan decomposition behind the Schubert stratification is computed.
Valuations. The radius function is a ratio of logarithms of valuations at a rank-one point, and the norm estimate of the closed-Cartier-divisor theorem is a valuation estimate on the Shilov boundary.
Spectral spaces. |Y_S| and |X_S| are locally spectral, the freeness and total discontinuity of the Frobenius action is a statement about specializations, and the quotient is again an adic space.
Localization. B = B^+[1/I_S] and A = W_{O_E}(R^+)[1/[varpi]]/xi are localizations, and the rational subsets defining the annuli are described by them.
Ideals and their generators. A primitive degree-one ideal is one generated by xi = p + [varpi]alpha, and the divisor of an ordered leg tuple is cut out by the product of such generators.
Graded algebras. P = sum_n H^0(X_S, O(n)) is one, and Proj of it is the algebraic curve.
The projective spectrum of a graded ring, the pinned carrier for Proj P; the basic opens D(g) on which the map of locally ringed spaces is defined are AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpen.
Locally ringed spaces. The map X_S -> X_S^alg is asserted at exactly this level of structure, and not as a map of schemes or of adic spaces.
Schemes. X_S^alg = Proj P is one, and the GAGA theorem of the bundles roadmap compares bundles on it with bundles on the adic curve.
Isocrystals, already pinned for E = Q_p. The functor to bundles on the curve is defined on this category, whose general-E version VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0 plans.
Monoidal categories. The functor from isocrystals to bundles is an exact TENSOR functor, which is what makes slopes additive.
Sheaves on a site. The sheafiness of the structure presheaf on the integral period space, the v-sheaf property of the divisor moduli, and the v-stack of bundles on a divisor are all statements here.
Grothendieck topologies, in which the v-topology and the analytic topology used for the local statements are expressed.
Quotients of categories, the nearest pinned form of the symmetric-group quotient defining the divisor moduli; the quotient there is taken inside v-sheaves and remains small.
The derived category. The Stein exhaustion argument concludes H^i(Y_S,F) = 0 for i > 0 through an R^1 lim vanishing, which is a derived statement.
Projective modules. Vector bundles on the annuli and on the divisors are finite projective modules over the corresponding rings.
Huber pairs. S = Spa(R,R^+), the annuli Spa(B_{S,I},B^+_{S,I}) and the divisor Spa(A,A^+) are all of this form, and the perfectoid Tate-Huber pair of the untilt correspondence is one too.
Spa of a Huber pair. The integral period space is literally Spa of the Witt ring minus a vanishing locus, so this is the pinned carrier of the roadmap's central object.
Invertible sheaves. The twists O_{X_S}(n), the Breuil-Kisin graded pieces I_S^m/I_S^{m+1} and the line bundle whose v-descent gives the unordered divisor ideal are all of this type.

nodes.title: Ramified Witt coefficients as the unique flat pi-adic lift
nodes.statement: For a perfect F_q-algebra R there is a unique pi-adically complete flat O_E-algebra R-tilde with R-tilde/pi = R, and a unique multiplicative section [.]: R -> R-tilde of the reduction. It is realised as W_{O_E}(R) = W(R) tensor-hat_{W(F_q)} O_E with pi-adic completion; when E = F_q((pi)) has equal characteristic this is R[[pi]].
hypotheses: R is a perfect F_q-algebra (perfectness is what makes the lift unique, not merely existent)
E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p, O_E its ring of integers, pi a chosen uniformizer
The tensor product W(R) tensor_{W(F_q)} O_E is completed pi-adically; without the completion the universal property fails
The equal-characteristic identification R[[pi]] uses the chosen uniformizer pi of E = F_q((pi))
proofSteps: Fargues-Scholze state the uniqueness of the pi-adically complete flat O_E-lift and of the Teichmueller section at the head of II.1.1, and then exhibit the lift as the pi-adically completed base change of p-typical Witt vectors along W(F_q) -> O_E.

The universal property in the form actually used later is the one invoked in the proof of Prop. II.1.2: for perfect R^+, maps W_{O_E}(R^+) -> A^+ into a pi-adically complete O_E-algebra correspond to maps R^+ -> (A^+)^flat.
The equal-characteristic case is read off from the formula, since W(R) tensor-hat_{W(F_q)} F_q[[pi]] = R[[pi]] for perfect R.
acceptance: Check on R = F_q that W_{O_E}(F_q) = O_E and [.] is the Teichmueller lift of the residue field
Check that for E ramified over Q_p the ring W_{O_E}(R) is NOT W(R) with p renamed: compare W_{O_E}(F_q-bar) = O_{E-breve} with W(F_q-bar) for E = Q_p(pi), pi^2 = p
Check the change-of-uniformizer comparison for two uniformizers pi, pi' of the same E

nodes.title: The integral period space Y-curly_S and independence of the pseudouniformizer
nodes.statement: For S = Spa(R,R^+) affinoid perfectoid over F_q and varpi in R^+ a pseudouniformizer, set Y-curly_S = Spa W_{O_E}(R^+) \ V([varpi]), where W_{O_E}(R^+) carries the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology. The result is independent of the choice of varpi, and the q-power Frobenius of R^+ induces an automorphism phi of Y-curly_S. The characteristic-p fibre V(pi) is retained: Y-curly_S is not base-changed to E.
hypotheses: S = Spa(R,R^+) affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p; R^+ open and integrally closed
varpi in R^+ a pseudouniformizer, i.e. a topologically nilpotent unit of R
W_{O_E}(R^+) is given the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology, not the pi-adic one; the removed locus is V([varpi]) only, not V(pi[varpi])
proofSteps: Fargues-Scholze define Y-curly_S in the affinoid case by removing V([varpi]) from Spa W_{O_E}(R^+) with the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology.
Independence of varpi is deduced from the divisibility relations varpi | varpi'^n and varpi' | varpi^n valid for any two pseudouniformizers of R, which give equality of the removed closed subsets.
The Frobenius automorphism is induced by functoriality of W_{O_E}(-) applied to the q-power Frobenius of R^+.
acceptance: Verify that V([varpi]) = V([varpi']) inside Spa W_{O_E}(R^+) for two pseudouniformizers
Verify on S = Spa(C,O_C) that the special fibre {pi = 0} of Y-curly_C is nonempty, so that Y-curly_S differs from Y_S
Verify that phi acts on Y-curly_S and fixes V(pi) setwise

sources.excerpt: we let Y-curly_S = Spa W_{O_E}(R^+) \ V([varpi]). Here W_{O_E}(R^+) has the (pi,[varpi])-adic topology. These objects do not depend on the choice of varpi, as for any choice of varpi, varpi' in R, one has varpi | varpi'^n, varpi' | varpi^n for some n > 0.

nodes.title: FS II.1.1: rational charts, perfectoid base change to O_{E_infty}, and sheafiness by splitting
nodes.statement: Y-curly_S is an analytic adic space over O_E. Letting E_infty be the completion of E(pi^{1/p^infty}), the base change Y-curly_S x_{Spa O_E} Spa O_{E_infty} is perfectoid, with tilt the perfectoid open unit disc S x_{F_q} Spa F_q[[t^{1/p^infty}]] = D_{S,perf}. Sheafiness of the structure presheaf on Y-curly_S is obtained from the perfectoid sheaf property because B_{S,[0,n]} splits off B_{S,[0,n]} tensor-hat_{O_E} O_{E_infty} as a topological direct factor.
hypotheses: S = Spa(R,R^+) affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p with pseudouniformizer varpi

The charts are the rational subsets Y-curly_{S,[0,n]} = {|pi|^n <= |[varpi]| != 0} of Spa W_{O_E}(R^+), n a positive integer taken to be a power of p; by applying Frobenius on (R,R^+) one may reduce to n = 1
B_{S,[0,n]} = W_{O_E}(R^+)<pi^n/[varpi]>[1/[varpi]], and B^+_{S,[0,n]} is the INTEGRAL CLOSURE of W_{O_E}(R^+)<pi^n/[varpi]> in B_{S,[0,n]}
E_infty is the completion of E(pi^{1/p^infty}) for the chosen uniformizer pi

Perfectoidness of A^+_0 is obtained from BMS18 Lemma 3.10(ii), which requires a ring pi-adically complete with respect to an element whose p-th power divides p, that element a nonzerodivisor, and Frobenius S/pi -> S/pi^p an isomorphism
proofSteps: Cover Y-curly_S by the rational subsets Y-curly_{S,[0,n]} of Spa W_{O_E}(R^+) and reduce to n = 1 using the Frobenius of (R,R^+).

Reduce the adic-space (sheafiness) claim to showing that A = B_{S,[0,1]} tensor-hat_{O_E} O_{E_infty} is a perfectoid Tate algebra: the map B_{S,[0,1]} -> A is split injective as topological B_{S,[0,1]}-modules, so the perfectoid sheaf property descends. Fargues-Scholze point to the sousperfectoid formalism of Hansen-Kedlaya and SW20 Section 6.3 for this step.

Set A^+_0 = (W_{O_E}(R^+) tensor-hat_{O_E} O_{E_infty})[(pi^{1/p^infty}/[varpi])]^wedge_{[varpi]} and compute A^+_0/[varpi] = (R^+/varpi tensor_{F_q} O_{E_infty}/pi)[t_1^{1/p^infty}]/(pi^{1/p^m} - [varpi]^{1/p^m} t_1^{1/p^m}) = R^+/varpi[t_1^{1/p^infty}].
Conclude A^+_0 is integral perfectoid by BMS18 Lemma 3.10(ii), then A^+_0 -> A^+ is an almost isomorphism and A = A^+_0[1/[varpi]] is perfectoid by BMS18 Lemma 3.21.
Identify the tilt of A as R<t_1^{1/p^infty}> with t_1^sharp = [varpi]/pi, corresponding to the locus {|t| <= |varpi| != 0} inside D_{S,perf}.
acceptance: Verify that B^+_{S,[0,n]} really is the integral closure and not the naive subring, on a base S whose R^+ is not a valuation ring
Verify the displayed computation of A^+_0/[varpi] on S = Spa(C,O_C) and on a non-field affinoid perfectoid S
Verify the topological splitting B_{S,[0,1]} -> B_{S,[0,1]} tensor-hat O_{E_infty} for ramified E/Q_p, where O_{E_infty}/O_E is not free

nodes.title: FS II.1.2: the diamond of the integral period space is Spd O_E x S
nodes.statement: For any perfectoid T over F_q, giving an untilt T^sharp of T together with a map T^sharp -> Y-curly_S of analytic adic spaces is the same as giving an untilt T^sharp with a map T^sharp -> Spa O_E and a map T -> S. Equivalently there is a natural isomorphism (Y-curly_S)^diamond = Spd O_E x S, and hence a natural map |Y-curly_S| -> |S|.
hypotheses: S = Spa(R,R^+) affinoid perfectoid over F_q; the argument reduces to affinoid T = Spa(A,A^+)
R^+ is perfect, so that the universal property of W_{O_E}(R^+) applies
The condition imposed on the map W_{O_E}(R^+) -> A^+ is that the image of [varpi] be invertible in A (this is what cuts out Y-curly_S, and it corresponds to invertibility of varpi in A^flat)
proofSteps: Reduce to: for T perfectoid over O_E, maps T -> Y-curly_S correspond to maps T^flat -> S.
A map T -> Y-curly_S is a map W_{O_E}(R^+) -> A^+ whose value on [varpi] is invertible in A.
Apply the universal property of W_{O_E}(R^+) for perfect R^+ to convert this into a map R^+ -> (A^+)^flat with varpi invertible in A^flat, i.e. a map Spa(A^flat,A^{flat+}) -> Spa(R,R^+).
The product Spd O_E x S is the product of v-sheaves on Perf_{F_q}; no structural morphism Y-curly_S -> S of adic spaces is asserted, only the map on topological spaces.
acceptance: Verify the claim for T = S^sharp an untilt of S itself, recovering the tautological section
Verify that the resulting map |Y-curly_S| -> |S| is the one used later to define the radius function
Check that the statement is about the diamond and does NOT produce an adic morphism Y-curly_S -> S

By the universal property of W_{O_E}(R^+) in case R^+ is perfect, this is equivalent to giving a map R^+ -> (A^+)^flat such that the image of varpi in A^flat is invertible.

nodes.title: FS II.1.3: open immersion and cartesian square for affinoid subsets of the base
nodes.statement: If S' is an affinoid subset of S then Y-curly_{S'} -> Y-curly_S is an open immersion, and the square (|Y-curly_{S'}| -> |Y-curly_S|, |S'| -> |S|) is cartesian. Consequently Y-curly_S can be defined for an arbitrary perfectoid space S by gluing, compatibly with the isomorphism (Y-curly_S)^diamond = Spd O_E x S.
hypotheses: S' a (not necessarily rational) affinoid subset of the affinoid perfectoid S

nodes.title: Untilts as primitive degree-one ideals in the Witt ring
nodes.statement: For (R,R^+) a perfectoid Tate-Huber pair of characteristic p, an untilt is the same as a primitive degree-one ideal J contained in W(R^+), i.e. one generated by an element xi = p + [varpi]alpha with varpi a pseudouniformizer of R^+ and alpha in W(R^+); any such xi is a nonzerodivisor. The correspondence sends (S,S^+) to (S^flat,S^{flat+}, ker theta) and (R,R^+,J) to (W(R^+)[1/[varpi]]/J, W(R^+)/J).
hypotheses: (R,R^+) is a perfectoid Tate-Huber pair of characteristic p
Primitivity of degree 1 is the shape xi = p + [varpi]alpha; the untilt is allowed to have characteristic p (take xi = p), so this does not force a characteristic-zero untilt
In Scholze-Weinstein this is stated for p-typical Witt vectors over Z_p; the ramified O_E-version replaces p by pi and W by W_{O_E}
proofSteps: Scholze-Weinstein prove that ker theta is generated by an explicit element of the required shape, constructed from f in varpi R^+ with f^sharp congruent to p modulo p varpi^sharp R^{sharp +}.
Nonzerodivisor property: assume xi sum [c_n]p^n = 0, reduce modulo [varpi] to get c_n congruent 0 modulo varpi, divide and induct.

Generation of ker theta: theta induces a surjection W(R^+)/xi -> R^{sharp +} which is an isomorphism modulo [varpi] because W(R^+)/(xi,[varpi]) = W(R^+)/(p,[varpi]) = R^+/varpi = R^{sharp +}/varpi^sharp.
Fargues-Scholze use the corresponding ramified normalisation xi = pi - a[varpi] in the proof of Prop. II.1.4.
acceptance: Verify the correspondence on the tautological untilt of R itself (xi = p), which must be allowed
Verify the ramified analogue of the shape xi = pi - a[varpi] for E ramified over Q_p
Verify that the plus ring of the untilt is W(R^+)/J and not merely the integral closure of the image

sources.excerpt: An ideal I contained in W(R^+) is primitive of degree 1 if I is generated by an element of the form xi = p + [varpi]alpha, with varpi in R^+ a pseudo-uniformizer and alpha in W(R^+). Lemma 6.2.10. Any element xi in W(R^+) of the form xi = p + [varpi]alpha ... is a nonzerodivisor.
sources.match: Exact definition and the nonzerodivisor lemma with its one-line induction proof.

sources.excerpt: There is an equivalence of categories between: 1. Perfectoid Tate-Huber pairs (S,S^+) 2. Triples (R,R^+,J), where (R,R^+) is a perfectoid Tate-Huber pair of characteristic p and J contained in W(R^+) is primitive of degree 1. In one direction the map is (S,S^+) -> (S^flat, S^{flat+}, ker theta), and in the other, it is (R,R^+,J) -> (W(R^+)[[varpi]^{-1}]/J, W(R^+)/J).
sources.match: The precise equivalence, including the formula for the plus ring.

sources.excerpt: We remark that there is no assumption that an untilt of R should have characteristic 0. In particular R itself is an untilt of R, corresponding to xi = p.
sources.match: Confirms that the characteristic-p untilt is retained, matching the stage text's insistence on keeping the special fibre.

nodes.title: FS II.1.4: an untilt is a closed Cartier divisor, via a Shilov-boundary norm estimate
nodes.statement: For S perfectoid over F_q, sections of (Y-curly_S)^diamond -> S, maps S -> Spd O_E, and untilts S^sharp of S over O_E are in natural bijection. Given such an untilt there is a natural closed immersion S^sharp -> Y-curly_S presenting S^sharp as a closed Cartier divisor: for U = Spa(A,A^+) contained in Y-curly_S with affinoid perfectoid pullback V = Spa(B,B^+) contained in S^sharp, the sequence 0 -> A --xi--> A -> B -> 0 is exact.
hypotheses: S = Spa(R,R^+) affinoid perfectoid; the generator may be chosen of the form xi = pi - a[varpi] with a in W_{O_E}(R^+), after choosing a pseudouniformizer varpi in R^+ with varpi^sharp | pi
One may localize near S^sharp = V(xi) and assume U = {|xi| <= |[varpi]|^n} for some n > 0
Norms are the spectral norms, normalized on each completed residue field of Y-curly_S by |[varpi]| = 1/q
The estimate |xi a| >= q^{-n}|a| for all a in A gives BOTH injectivity and closed image; surjectivity onto B uses that R^sharp is the separated completion of A/xi

The maximum-modulus step is reduced to the Shilov boundary, then to U x_{Spa O_E} Spa O_{E_infty}, then to the tilt, an affinoid subset of D_{S,perf}, and finally by approximation to classical affinoid subsets of D_S
proofSteps: Deduce the bijection (i)-(iii) directly from Prop. II.1.2.
Write R^{sharp +} = W_{O_E}(R^+)/xi with xi = pi - a[varpi] obtained from pi = varpi^sharp theta(a).

To prove exactness, localize so that U = {|xi| <= |[varpi]|^n}; prove |xi a| >= q^{-n}|a| using that the spectral norm on U is the supremum over the Shilov boundary, all of whose points lie in {|xi| = |[varpi]|^n}.
Transfer the maximum principle through the split base change to O_{E_infty} and the tilt to D_{S,perf}, then approximate by classical affinoid subsets of D_S where the maximum principle is classical.
Conclude injectivity and closedness of the image of xi, and identify B = A/xi.
acceptance: Verify the inequality |xi a| >= q^{-n}|a| on an explicit annulus for E = Q_p and for a ramified E
Verify the normalization |[varpi]| = 1/q and that changing varpi rescales but does not destroy the estimate
Verify the existence of varpi with varpi^sharp | pi on a non-field affinoid perfectoid base

nodes.title: Div^1 = Spd E/phi^Z: degree-one divisors, properness and cohomological smoothness
nodes.statement: A closed Cartier divisor of degree 1 on X_S is by definition one arising from a map S -> Spd(E)/phi^Z, equivalently locally on S from an untilt S^sharp over E. The moduli space of such is Div^1 = Spd(E)/phi^Z, where the quotient may be computed either as a v-sheaf quotient or for the topology of open covers, so that 'locally on S' may be read v-locally or on open subsets of |S|. The map Div^1 -> * is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, and cohomologically smooth.
hypotheses: E is the fixed nonarchimedean local coefficient field; over Perf_k with k algebraically closed, Spd(E) is replaced by Spd(E-breve) and Div^1 = Spd(E-breve)/phi^Z

Cohomological smoothness of Spd(E) -> * is quoted from ECD Proposition 24.5 for E = Q_p, from which the finite-extension case follows formally; the equal-characteristic case is handled inside that proof
Properness is obtained from the valuative criterion of ECD Proposition 18.3 after qcqs-ness is established
Div^1 is the moduli of degree-1 divisors, not the curve itself; FS flag this explicitly
proofSteps: Sections of (Y_S)^diamond -> S correspond to maps S -> Spd E and to untilts over E (Prop. II.1.18, from II.1.4).
Composing S^sharp -> Y_S -> X_S still gives a closed Cartier divisor depending only on S -> Spd(E)/phi^Z, giving the injection of Spd(E)/phi^Z into closed Cartier divisors on X_S.
|Spd(E) x S| = |Y_S| -> |S| together with total discontinuity of phi^Z gives |Spd(E)/phi^Z x S| = |X_S| -> |S| qcqs for qcqs S, hence representability in spatial diamonds.
Properness then follows from the valuative criterion; cohomological smoothness is inherited from Spd(E) -> *.
acceptance: Verify Div^1(C) = untilts of C over E modulo Frobenius, matching Def./Prop. II.1.22
Verify that the open-cover quotient and the v-sheaf quotient agree, so that a degree-1 divisor is analytically local on S

nodes.statement: Fix an algebraically closed k over F_q and let E-breve = W_{O_E}(k)[1/pi] with Frobenius sigma. Functorially in S in Perf_k there is a natural exact tensor-functor Isoc_k -> Bun(X_S), (D,phi) -> E(D,phi), obtained by descending D tensor_{E-breve} O_{Y_S} along phi tensor phi. One sets O_{X_S}(n) = E(E-breve, pi^{-n} sigma); the functor REVERSES slopes, and for the simple isocrystal (D_lambda, phi_lambda) of slope lambda one sets O_{X_S}(-lambda) = E(D_lambda, phi_lambda).
